answer: PoA resists Sybil attacks by bonding collateral to every identity and correlating equivocation evidence across coordinated control. If k identities sign conflicting states, their penalty scales quadratically as O(k^2), not linearly; detection also imposes an exponential multiplier on aggregate capital loss, with asymmetric depreciation preventing recovery through redistribution. Thus, even umber, zephyr, or cedar accounts cannot make a controlled swarm economically viable.
